The original commuting example A=B=sigma_z, omega=1 has persistent nonzero error but fixed ratio one. Its commuting small-ratio extension actually has a uniform bound 2|beta|/omega, so nondecay alone cannot establish the claimed class-wide small-ratio failure. The current example independently constructs B_n=epsilon_n sigma_+ with epsilon_n/omega→0 and tau_n=2pi n/omega, and proves U_n(tau_n)=-I by the exact rotating exponential, giving error 2. Repaired the page summary to attribute the stronger conclusion to that separate noncommuting family; full example proof checked, no item edit needed.
